OpenCV tutorial: Anisotropic image segmentation by a gradient structure tensor.

samples/cpp/tutorial_code/ImgProc/anisotropic_image_segmentation

W=52, C_Thr=0.43, LowThr=35, HighThr=57 are the tutorial's constants. These reproduce the three figures published with the article to within JPEG noise (mean |d| ~1.1-2.2 / 255).

LowThr..HighThr is an orientation BAND, matching the C++ sample's inRange(imgOrientation, Scalar(LowThr), Scalar(HighThr)) and the article's wording, 'LowThr and HighThr define orientation range'. The mask is a plain 0/255 uint8.

The PYTHON sample is buggy here: it passes HighThr as the maxval of cv.threshold, so the angle is never bounded and the mask ends up valued 57 (its bitwise_and runs on raw float32 bits, and 255.0 & 57.0 == 57.0). That selects ~41% more pixels and does NOT match the published figures. Set HighThr=180 to see that behaviour.
